new_jobs.title: Certified Community Health Worker - CKD
new_jobs.description:
Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM (1 - hour lunch)

Compensation : $40,000 - $50,000 a year (May increase based on experience) CHW Certification Required for this role.

Job Summary

The Community Health Worker goes beyond medicine by connecting AbsoluteCare members with resources that help address their social needs and overcome barriers to care. This role fosters trust and builds meaningful relationships with members, meeting them wherever they are, whether at home, in the community, at the hospital, or in an office setting. The Community Health Worker will also reach out to new members, educating them about AbsoluteCare and guiding them through enrollment in both internal and external services. This position operates in a matrixed environment, with dual reporting to the Community Team Care Manager for daily care management and the Engagement Manager/Director for performance evaluation, strategic alignment, and program oversight.

Duties And Responsibilities

Effectively represent AbsoluteCare, and communicate how ABC’s services, programs, and resources, including ABC’s PCP clinical care model—can help in the member’s specific situation.
Conduct in-person non-clinical assessments to understand member needs, preferences, and barriers to care, including social determinants of health (SDOH), and evaluate the home environment as needed.
Create and administer individualized care plans for members, incorporating clinical team input when addressing clinical needs.
Effectively and efficiently connect members with appropriate AbsoluteCare and community resources such as mental health, substance abuse, housing support, transportation, clothing, food, and other basic needs.
Authentically build trust and rapport with members, their support systems, and communities to drive engagement.
Manage a caseload of members, identifying and addressing member needs, enrolling members in appropriate services, and ensuring follow-through on care plans and connections to community and clinical resources.
Partner with care team (community PCPs, specialists, and internal staff), including attending daily huddles and team meetings, prioritizing members, caseload, and align around actions.
Document daily outreach activities into care management platforms (e.g., Jiva), electronic health records (e.g., eCW), and CRM systems.
Meet predefined metrics and KPIs for successful member engagement, social needs resolution, and member enrollment into programs and services
Support members within the Member Lounge with events.

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required.
Must have a valid driver’s license, proof of insurance, and reliable personal vehicle.
2+ years of experience working with community agency providing services encompassing the basic competency areas of health care (community resources, communication skills, individual and family advocacy, health education, services skills, and responsibilities).
CPR/BLS certification required.
Certified as a Community Health Worker required prior to employment
Experience and passion for working with and engaging vulnerable, hard to engage, complex populations.
Independent and persistent self-starter
Proficient in PC skills, such as Microsoft Office.
Ability to travel locally at a minimum of 80% of the time.
Knowledge and trusting relationships within the local community, and experience and knowledge navigating community resources.

Working conditions

This job operates in the community, in members’ homes, and in the AbsoluteCare clinical center. This role requires a dedicated, quiet workspace with the ability to adhere to HIPAA and other privacy policies. A reliable and high-speed Wi-Fi connection. This role routinely uses general office equipment. It is required that you have and can use your personal vehicle to conduct outreach including member home visits.

Physical Requirements

Driving and walking in the community where our members live.
Ability to communicate clearly and exchange accurate information constantly.
Ability to remain stationary for long periods of time.
Ability to operate computer, keyboard, copy and fax machine, phone, and other general office equipment.
Ability to occasionally move objects up to 20 lbs.

Direct reports

None.

All Employees are expected to maintain the security and privacy of all information that is owned by AbsoluteCare or maintained on behalf of the company’s patients, employees, and business partners. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. This description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions, it does not proscribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned. This job description is subject to change at any time.

new_jobs.description:
Category

Customer Care/Customer Service

Job Location

5945 Cornhusker Highway, Suite D, Lincoln, Nebraska

Tracking Code

15651-128

Position Type

Full-Time/Regular

At Numotion, we’re on a mission to improve the lives of people with disabilities. As North America’s largest provider of mobility products and services, we deliver personalized solutions from manual and power wheelchairs to medical supplies and other assistive technologies that support health, independence, and everyday participation. We’re committed to a workforce of diverse backgrounds and experiences and to an inclusive environment shaped by open dialogue, attentive listening, and tangible, ongoing action.

Job Purpose

Receives and implements new equipment requests, determines reimbursement eligibility and coordinates the timely provision of services. Facilitates timely order movement through Numotion’s order processing system.

Key Responsibilities

Assists customers with new equipment requests, obtains demographics, enters and maintains accurate data in order processing system while progressing orders through to completion.
Verifies insurance/funding eligibility and benefits, communicates to customers their financial responsibility, obtains prescriptions and any other medical documentation necessary to obtain funding.
Enters orders into order processing system assuring that efforts are made to accurately and completely perform intake steps.
Responds to customer inquiries, requests, and complaints in a timely manner working with other staff members to increase customer satisfaction and turnaround times.
Takes responsibility to completely resolve issues without additional transfers and/or de-escalate customers whenever possible.
Coordinates scheduling of ATP’s and seating technicians for evaluations and adjustments requests.
Meets all set productivity and performance standards
Participates in New Equipment department initiatives to continually improve department results.
Other duties as assigned by manager
Utilize Numotion Leadership Principles to perform job with integrity, compliance, and values consistent with Numotion’s mission.
Adhere to employee or customer confidentiality and comply with Numotion’s policies and federal regulations.
Provide excellent customer service for all internal and external customers of the operations at all times. Provide solutions for customer concerns and continually focus on customer service as our top priority.
The above duties and responsibilities are not an all-inclusive list but rather a general representation of the duties and responsibilities associated with this position. The duties and responsibilities will be subject to change based on organizational needs and/or as deemed necessary by management.

Required Qualifications, Skills, And Experience

High school diploma or general education degree (GED) or equivalent combination of experience and education.
Minimum one year of customer service experience.

Preferred Competencies And Qualifications

Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
Strong listening, organization and priority setting skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and juggle multiple priorities.
Ability to think quickly, assess a situation and make a sound decision.
Ability to provide best-in-class customer service
Working knowledge of service order processing experience
Knowledge of complex rehab equipment and products
Prior experience working in durable medical equipment industry
Demonstration of exceptional interpersonal and problem-solving skills both internally and externally with customers.
Knowledge of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

Physical Work Requirements

The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Frequent use of hands, wrists, fingers associated with computer equipment.
Prolonged periods of time working at a desk and/or on a computer.
Occasionally move and reach with arms and hands.
Ability to communicate effectively.
Ability to work overtime as needed.

At Numotion, we offer competitive compensation packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, short-term and long-term disability, a 401k, and life insurance. Numotion is an equal opportunity employer. We strive for a workplace that reflects the communities we serve and do not tolerate discrimination against our employees, customers, and partners regardless of ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, citizenship, marital or veteran status. Numotion is a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment.

new_jobs.title: Patient Advocate / Care Manager (Private Health Advisor)
new_jobs.description:
The Short Version

You will carry six to eight families. Not sixty. Not two hundred.

Part-time and hourly, or full-time and salaried: W-2 either way, and yours to grow at your own pace.

We have removed insurance mandates and hospital bureaucracy from the work. What that buys you is the rarest thing in modern medicine: the time to do the job the way you already know it should be done.

If that is the job you have been looking for, here is the rest of it.

The Role

Avoa Health is a private health advisory firm serving families on Chicago’s North Shore through serious diagnoses, complex conditions, and the challenges of aging. The Private Health Advisor is the single, trusted point of contact for those families. Their advocate. Their Healthcare Chief of Staff. The person who sees the problem coming before they do.

This is not case management. Case management is a caseload. This is a small number of families, held closely, over time.

Our clients are accustomed to excellence in every other part of their lives, and they expect the same standard here. One size fits one: every family receives a response built for them alone.

What You Will Do

Run central command.
You are the connective tissue between the family and their specialists, making sure every provider is aligned and the client’s agency is protected. You manage the scheduling, the records, the follow-up. Hushpitality is our word for doing that invisibly: the family experiences the result of your work without ever carrying the noise of it.
Vet the specialists. You evaluate physicians and institutions and find the right fit, not the nearest one.

Show up in the room.
You accompany clients to the appointments that matter, with the agenda prepared in advance, and you deliver a post-visit summary that turns jargon into a clear path forward.

Dismantle the roadblocks.
Pre-authorizations, denials, billing disputes. You absorb that friction so the family never feels it.

Build the scaffolding.
For clients facing cognitive decline or a difficult transition, you put discreet systems in place that preserve dignity while keeping them safe.

Own the problem.
Every issue is yours. When the system fails, you listen, you own it, and you fix it. You never say it is not your department.

Who This is For

You have five or more years in healthcare, ideally in advocacy, case management, oncology navigation, palliative care, or geriatric care. LPN, RN, or MSW is preferred and not mandatory.
You are warm. You are conscientious to the point that other people find it remarkable. You assume things will work out and you make them work out.

You can move from a technical conversation with a neurosurgeon to a briefing with a family office director without changing gear.

Your language is precise and generous. You know the difference between “I’ll try” and “I will see to it,” and so does the family listening.

You are comfortable with modern tools: secure video, shared calendars, the ordinary technology of a well-run firm. We provide the technology and the administrative backing so your attention stays on the families.

The Deal

Part-time roles are hourly. Full-time roles are salaried.
Both are W-2, which makes you a formal member of the team, not a contractor.
It grows at your pace.
Start part-time and grow into full-time as you and your client book are ready, or stay part-time for as long as it fits your life. Both are real, long-term seats.
Real control over your schedule, in both directions
. If you cannot take Tuesday mornings, we will not book you Tuesday mornings. In return, we ask for dependable daytime availability, since most of the work, care coordination and physician visits, happens in business hours, plus a willingness to help with the occasional off-hours emergency, which the team shares and covers together. We ask every advisor to hold at least one full day a week for Avoa Health, because that predictability is what lets us balance the work and protect everyone’s schedule. What you will not have is a pager, a quota, or a productivity metric.
Hybrid, roughly seventy percent remote
and thirty percent in person, flexing with what clients need. Our clients are concentrated on the North Shore, so plan on in-person meetings and physician visits in that area.
Travel is covered
. You will drive to client appointments; mileage between them is reimbursed at the standard IRS rate, and a company card covers authorized work expenses.
You are supported, not on your own
. Malpractice and liability coverage, secure technology, and full administrative backing, so your attention stays on the families rather than the overhead.
Full transparency before you invest an hour.
Before any formal interview, we put every parameter of the role in writing for you: compensation, schedule, technology, and the health and screening requirements. You will know exactly what you are considering before you commit your time. We think that is the only respectful way to do this.

Why Avoa Health

A return to the art of care
. You went into this work to help people, and somewhere along the way volume took the helping out of it. There is no volume here.

Autonomy with infrastructure
. You manage your own client portfolio. You operate with the independence of a private practitioner and none of the isolation, supported by the firm's systems and reputation.

Going above and beyond is the standard, and it is funded
. When you see what a family needs, you will not have to ask permission or find the budget.

Depth
. A handful of families, known well, over years. That is the entire proposition.

About Rocksolid

Rocksolid Community Teen Center transforms lives through positive youth development, mentorship, and growth. We provide teens with a safe, welcoming place to build relationships, confidence, life skills, and community connection.

Position Summary

The Program Manager leads Rocksolid’s day-to-day teen programming and creates a safe, structured, welcoming, and engaging experience for youth. This position oversees daily program operations, activities, staff assistants, volunteers, transportation, parent communication, teen support, camps, attendance, and program outcomes. The Program Manager works closely with the Executive Director to carry out organizational priorities and maintain consistent program policies and procedures.

Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesProgram Planning and Daily Operations

• Develop and maintain the annual program calendar, daily activity schedule, and plans for camps, field trips, and special program experiences.
• Plan and lead engaging, age-appropriate activities aligned with Rocksolid’s mission and positive youth development approach.
• Manage daily opening, closing, setup, cleanup, supplies, snacks, meals, check-in, check-out, attendance, and parent authorization procedures.
• Create opportunities for teen leadership, youth voice, feedback, and meaningful participation.
• Maintain accurate activity, permission, attendance, transportation, and program participation records.

Teen Safety, Support, and Behavior Management

• Create an environment where teens are treated with dignity, fairness, consistency, and respect while maintaining clear expectations and healthy boundaries.
• Monitor teen behavior, use appropriate de-escalation strategies, respond to concerns, and support positive youth development.
• Review registration information regarding IEPs, 504 Plans, disabilities, medical, behavioral, sensory, communication, mobility, or other support needs that may affect participation.
• Work with families and the Executive Director to develop support, accommodation, behavior, and safety plans when needed.
• Document behavioral, medical, transportation, and safety incidents promptly; communicate serious concerns to parents and the Executive Director.
• Lead immediate emergency response during program hours and ensure staff readiness through established safety procedures and drills.

Staff, Volunteer, and Transportation Leadership

• Recruit, interview, onboard, schedule, supervise, coach, and evaluate Staff Assistants in coordination with the Executive Director.
• Recruit, orient, train, schedule, and supervise program volunteers and interns.
• Assign daily roles, provide clear direction, model professional conduct, and ensure appropriate adult coverage and supervision ratios.
• Develop school pickup routes and transportation schedules and coordinate approved drivers and van coverage.
• Ensure transportation lists, emergency contacts, permissions, vehicle capacity, and parent communication are complete before pickups or outings.
• Report performance concerns, vehicle issues, facility hazards, maintenance needs, or significant safety concerns to the Executive Director.

Parent, School, and Community Communication

• Serve as the primary contact for routine parent questions regarding attendance, activities, behavior, transportation, camps, and daily program matters.
• Communicate clearly, professionally, and compassionately while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate boundaries.
• Coordinate school outreach and student recruitment and maintain relationships with counselors and frontline school staff.
• Coordinate teen stories, displays, performances, or program participation at fundraising and community events as requested.
• Refer complaints, legal concerns, media inquiries, major partnership requests, and sensitive organizational matters to the Executive Director.

Program Outcomes and Organizational Coordination

• Collect teen feedback, program stories, participation data, and outcome information that demonstrate program quality and impact.
• Track program goals, identify trends and barriers, and recommend opportunities for program improvement.
• Prepare timely program updates and reports for the Executive Director and, when requested, the Board of Directors.
• Coordinate with the Assistant Director to ensure program forms, records, calendar information, and communications are complete and organized.
• Participate in staff meetings, planning, training, community events, and other duties consistent with the role.

Required Qualifications

• At least two years of experience working directly with middle school or high school youth in a structured program setting; supervisory or lead experience strongly preferred.
• Demonstrated ability to plan engaging activities, manage groups, establish consistent expectations, and respond calmly to challenging behavior or emergencies.
• Strong communication, organization, documentation, judgment, relationship-building, and follow-through skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively with teens, families, staff, volunteers, schools, community partners, and organizational leadership.
• Proficiency with common digital tools for scheduling, attendance, forms, documents, email, and program reporting.
• Commitment to Rocksolid’s mission; successful background check; valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record. Must meet Rocksolid requirements when operating organization vehicles.
• Current First Aid/CPR certification, or ability to obtain certification within the timeframe established by Rocksolid.

Preferred Qualifications

• Associate or bachelor’s degree in youth development, education, social services, recreation, nonprofit management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
• Experience supervising staff, interns, or volunteers in a youth-serving nonprofit, school, church, recreation, or community organization.
• Experience supporting youth with behavioral, medical, disability, sensory, communication, or accommodation needs.
• Experience coordinating school transportation, camps, field trips, or community-based youth activities.

Physical and Scheduling Requirements

This active, youth- and community-based position requires regular supervision of teens in indoor, outdoor, gym, transportation, and field-trip settings; effective in-person and electronic communication; frequent standing and movement throughout program spaces; and occasional lifting or movement of program materials or supplies weighing approximately 25 pounds. The anticipated start date is mid-August 2026. The regular schedule is approximately 25 hours per week, generally five hours per day Monday-Friday during afternoon and early evening program hours, with occasional adjusted hours for camps, field trips, meetings, or special events.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Rocksolid Community Teen Center is an equal opportunity employer committed to a welcoming, inclusive, and respectful environment and does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics under applicable law.

This description outlines the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of duties or qualifications. Rocksolid may modify responsibilities as program and organizational needs evolve.

Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

As AI Legal Program Manager, you will play a key role in navigating the legal and regulatory landscape of Block's artificial intelligence initiatives. You will partner with legal, engineering, product, and compliance teams to develop frameworks that enable responsible AI innovation while ensuring regulatory compliance and risk management across our AI products and services.
You will:
Drive the development and implementation of AI legal and compliance frameworks, including policies for model development, deployment, and monitoring that align with emerging AI regulations and industry standards.

Strong understanding of emerging AI regulations (EU AI Act, state AI laws, etc.) and their practical implementation.
Experience developing legal frameworks for AI governance and responsible AI development.
Track record of partnering with technical teams to implement legal requirements in AI systems.
Understanding of IP considerations in AI development, including training data rights, model ownership, and output licensing.
Experience with AI risk assessment methodologies and mitigation strategies.
Strong project management skills with experience leading cross-functional initiatives.

Even better:
Experience with large language models (LLMs) and generative AI legal considerations
Background in open source software licensing and AI model licensing
Familiarity with AI ethics frameworks and algorithmic fairness principles
Experience with AI procurement and vendor assessment
Knowledge of global AI regulatory developments and policy trends
Background in privacy law and data protection regulations
Technical background or demonstrated ability to understand AI/ML concept

new_jobs.description:
Title:
Case Manager

Program:
Willow Tree Residence

Salary Range:
$42,290-$46,290 per year

Program Description

Willow Tree Residence is a 130-unit congregate care supportive housing program located in East Midtown Manhattan. The facility is unique in that it is co-located with a women’s shelter that occupies the first 6 floors of a 21-story building and offers a street facing Article 28 clinic on the first floor dedicated to providing primary and behavioral health care services. Willow Tree provides 79 permanent, supportive housing units for chronically homeless single adults with a serious mental illness [SMI], a substance use disorder [SUD], or those who may have a co-occurring SMI and SUD. Candidates are referred through the Department of Homeless services [DHS]; however, the facility is funded by DOHMH. The remaining 51 units are “fair market” and reserved for low-income tenants, referred from the local community.

Overall Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Clinical Director and the Program Director, the Case Manager conducts required assessments, general case management and direct care services to clients. In this role, the Case Manager supports clients in addressing identified needs, building the skills and stability necessary to regulate their lives, achieve greater independence, and transition to permanent housing or other appropriate community-based housing options. The Case Manager also provides referrals and links clients to appropriate internal and external resources, assists with other cases as needed, and ensures all required protocols are followed. The Case Manager maintains client charts in accordance with program standards and ensures documentation remains complete, accurate, and audit-ready at all times, and performs other related duties as assigned.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The essential duties of the Case Manager include, but are not limited to, the following activities:

Provides case management services and assists clients in the creation of and adherence to their Service Plans by identifying short and long-term objectives that can be achieved.
Conducts intake and assessments, makes necessary referrals for services, and completes/updates psycho-social assessments of tenants.
Provides direct services, linkage to services and coordination of services for Willow Tree residents.
Counsel residents on money management, medication management, daily living activities and housing maintenance.
Accompany and advocate on behalf of the residents with community-based services, as needed.
Create and lead groups addressing functional and psychosocial needs of residents.
Participate in weekly clinical team meetings and receive individual supervision.
Inputs all client information and updates in a timely fashion into the AWARDS system as well as the client’s physical chart
Maintains accurate and up-to-date written client documentation as required and in accordance with City/State oversight agency guidelines.
Maintains liaison with representatives from community organizations
Performs other duties as assigned by the Team Leader, Director of Social Services, and/or Program Director
While performing the duties of this position, the Clinical Director must stand to talk to clients and staff, sit for extended periods of time at the computer, and reach or squat to get records from the files.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
An Associate’s degree with three (2) years of experience working with homeless, mentally ill and chemically addicted individuals or other special needs populations.
Ability to work cooperatively with peers and other staff to serve the needs of the clients as effectively and efficiently as possible.
Excellent oral, writing, and listening skills are a must.
The ability to work well within a highly pressurized, deadline environment, while meeting the short-term and long-term mandates of the program.
An ability to interface with clients as well as all levels of staff.
Knowledge of case management software as well as proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
Bilingual or multilingual a plus.

Job Description

The Iowa Vocational Rehabilitation Team at Iowa Workforce Development is accepting applications for full-time Special Programming Workforce Program Coordinator role in our Iowa WORKS offices.

This position currently serves in the role of project manager for the Disability Innovation Fund Subminimum Wage to Competitive Integrated Employment (DIF-SWTCIE) Grant program; however, it is a permanent position with the Vocational Rehabilitation Division of Iowa Workforce Development and will continue post-grant focused on coordination of the ongoing services, supports, and best practices that were implemented through the grant initiatives.

Domicile will be determined based on the hired candidate’s location at one of our Iowa Works centers.

Job Description And Responsibilities

Coordinate, manage, and oversee the Disability Innovation Fund Subminimum Wage to Competitive Integrated Employment (DIF-SWTCIE) Grant program, based on the established DIF Workplan. Communicate with the IWD communication team for branding, marketing, and website for the DIF-SWTCIE grant. Coordinate Collective and Steering Committee meetings, as well as the associated work groups. Provide oversight of DIF-SWTCIE pilot projects and ensure progress, dissemination, and evaluation of each project. Ensure all expenditures, programs, services, and activities are ended at the completion of the grant, in alignment with RSA guidance.

Draft and submit required reporting for the DIF-SWTCIE grant, including end-of-year reports, annual reports, monthly reports, and other requested documents. Ensure successful submission of documents into the appropriate systems. Coordinate with relevant IVRS staff on the review of DIF-SWTICE data to inform grant progress and prepare reports and other requests for DIF-SWTCIE data.

Manage and administer contracts and agreements with vendors related to the DIF-SWTCIE grant (e.g., GHA, CEA, DB101, CEBH, etc.) and IPS and CE services, in accordance with state contracting requirements and federal regulations. Provide consultation and technical assistance to CRPs and IVRS staff to ensure compliance with DIF-SWTCIE and WIOA requirements. Provide recommendations to IVRS Executive Team on necessary program improvements. Identify quality indicators; facilitate, initiate and execute agreements with partners, problem-solve and negotiate on behalf of IVRS to expand training opportunities and program success. Serve on the Contract Oversight and Review Experts (CORE) committee to provide updates on contracts.

Participate in internal and external initiatives that impact employment outcomes for individuals with disabilities who may participate in IPS, CE and/or DIF services. Develop standards for delivering current or new services, as well as procedures for monitoring current or new services, including necessary approvals. Represent the work of the DIF grant in coordination with the State Rehabilitation Council.

Collaborate with all levels of IVRS staff on the development and recommendation of policies that impact services, including IPS and CE. Coordinate with the Supported Employment Resource Manager to ensure the SES manual is in alignment with guidance provided on CE and IPS. Attend associated meetings (e.g., State Rehabilitation Council, IMPACT, etc.) to represent both the DIFSWTCIE grant and associated services.

Serve as the Intermediary for the Direct Support Professional (DSP) Registered Apprenticeship and any associated pre-apprenticeships. Ensure necessary agreements are in place with businesses, schools, and other associated parties. Other duties as assigned.

The successful candidate must be able to pass a criminal background check conducted by the Iowa Department of Public Safety.

About Iowa Workforce Development

Iowa Workforce Development (IWD) is a state agency dedicated to providing exceptional employment services and connecting employers with skilled workers.
